Caption: 



----------
howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy tuesday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* AI is getting better at building the next AI

* OpenAI’s new model is solving unsolved maths problems

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…


----------

----------
#### **WISPR FLOW**

## [Walk-and-think (capture ideas on the move)](https://ref.wisprflow.ai/aivalley)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9eb4e047-5486-4a71-8a19-9c795a8f1c91/Newsletters_Image_1920x1080__7___7_.png?t=1790084998)
Follow image link: (https://ref.wisprflow.ai/aivalley)
Caption: Courtesy: Wispr Flow

Some problems don't solve themselves at a keyboard. Flow is perfect for walks: talk through the idea, the structure, the tradeoffs—then get back a clean draft you can paste into your doc or AI tool. It's like having a writing assistant that keeps up with your brain in motion.

[Try Flow Free](https://ref.wisprflow.ai/aivalley)

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

**1/ AI is getting better at building the next AI** - OpenAI has apparently automated training experimental models, according to [The Information](https://x.com/kimmonismus/status/2102168154973614087?s=20), while Anthropic says AI now leads [~26% of its R&D work](https://www.anthropic.com/institute/measuring-pace-of-ai-development) and collaborates on 90%.

This is getting into “recursive self-improvement” territory. Basically, AI helps build a better AI, which then gets better at building the next one, and you repeat. It’s an old idea (goes back to the 1950s) and one of the ways people think AI progress could suddenly get very fast.

We’re not there yet, though. Current models still can’t really run this loop without humans, and some of what we’re seeing might just be very good coding automation.

But the pace is getting insane. In 2022, models struggled with basic arithmetic. By 2023, they could pass the bar exam. In 2024, they were writing decent software and doing graduate-level science. By late 2025, some top engineers were saying AI was doing most of their coding. And the models arriving in 2026 are another pretty big jump.

[METR](https://metr.org/) has a nice way of tracking this. They measure how long a task would take a human expert, then see whether an AI can do the whole thing on its own. That went from ~10-minute tasks to an hour, then several hours. Claude Opus 4.5 was at nearly 5 hours, with the number roughly doubling every 7 months (and recent data suggests maybe closer to 4).

And that doesn’t include the newest models yet.

**2/ OpenAI’s new model is apparently solving unsolved maths problems** - OpenAI [says](https://openai.com/index/advisory-group-on-mathematics-and-ai/) an internal model it started training just 24 days ago has already resolved 100+ long-standing open problems across maths, including the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem. Apparently, the pace surprised even its own mathematicians.

So they’ve put together an independent advisory group with some pretty serious mathematicians, including Edward Witten, Timothy Gowers and Martin Hairer. They’ll help review the results, figure out how/when to release them and basically tell OpenAI when they think it’s doing something wrong. They’re unpaid and can publicly disagree with the company too.

There’s already some pushback from mathematicians about AI labs treating unsolved problems as benchmarks. Fair enough when your 24-day-old model is apparently knocking out problems people have been stuck on for years.


----------

----------
# TRENDING TOOLS


--------------------
* [Acrobat's new AI](https://business.adobe.com/products/acrobat-business.html) - helps you understand documents faster, turning dense reports into visual summaries, interactive reports, podcasts, and audio experiences you can take anywhere ~^(sponsored)^~

* [Akai](https://x.com/Bouazizalex/status/2102127902510944722?s=20) - an internal tool to automate our painfully repetitive operations in Finance, HR, Accounts Payable, and Compliance, etc

* [Pexo](https://x.com/Pexoai_offical/status/2102020852984471993?s=20) - AI video agent. You can create videos the way you vibe-code

* [Grok 4.7](https://x.com/SpaceXAI/status/2102069815225586149?s=20) - a notable improvement over Grok 4.6 at the same price and speed

* [Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6](https://x.com/XiaomiMiMo/status/2102138559952290106?s=20) - debuts as a new top open-weight model, built for complex projects, long-horizon tasks, high-stakes work, cybersecurity, and research

* [Motion](https://x.com/motion_so/status/2101743483123892677?s=20) - introduced Muse but for motion design

* [Codos](https://x.com/dimakhanarin/status/2102065316406997475?s=20) - the virtual Chief AI Officer. It interviews employees, deploys automations across all functions and gets smarter over time while running on your own servers

* [Adam and Eve](https://x.com/TungaBayrak/status/2102069626762932680?s=20) - the most human-like AI voices ever built

* [Origami](https://x.com/origamichat/status/2102079089049804927?s=20) - launches ChatGPT-6 Astra for sales. Simply enter your website URL, and Origami will reach out to thousands of customers promoting your product in seconds, across every single channel

* [AskJev](https://askjev.net/) - Have a question? Ask Jev

* [slop-grader](https://github.com/lukstei/slop-grader) - checks every line against your own writing rules, flags high-confidence violations, and returns structured results an agent can use to rewrite them


----------

----------
# WHAT I'M CONSUMING


--------------------
* How much is [AI really going to change ](https://www.reddit.com/r/ArtificialInteligence/comments/1r8p2gb/how_much_is_ai_really_going_to_change_the_near/)the near future (5-20years)?

* [Jev explained](https://x.com/matthewcanham/status/2102077098756280413) for normies

* Why I [changed my mind](https://www.persuasion.community/p/why-i-changed-my-mind-about-ai-risk?r=ifpt&utm_campaign=post-expanded-share&utm_medium=web&triedRedirect=true) about AI risk

* The [business](https://www.strangeloopcanon.com/p/the-business-of-building-god) of building God

* OpenAI [said to develop](https://www.theinformation.com/newsletters/ai-agenda/openai-develops-features-counter-grok-bot-mulls-response-metas-muse?rc=u2tpxn) Grok Bot rival, discussed personal AI assistant to challenge Meta’s Muse

* Amazon [blacks](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/amazon-blocks-metas-muse-ai-assistant-in-new-standoff-over-agentic-shopping/) Meta’s Muse agent off from shopping on Amazon only 12 days after launch

----------
howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy monday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* One of ChatGPT’s inventors thinks AI talks too much

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…


----------

----------
#### **DIIO**

## [AI that understands what business conversations are trying to achieve](https://www.diio.com/us/starter-diio?utm_source=ai_valley&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ai_valley_2026&utm_content=2026-09-21&utm_term=main_ad_starter)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/648aa55e-4bb0-4df3-82a7-9ba2c84ccdf6/diio-AI-Valley__1_.png?t=1789997380)
Follow image link: (https://www.diio.com/us/starter-diio?utm_source=ai_valley&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ai_valley_2026&utm_content=2026-09-21&utm_term=main_ad_starter)
Caption: Courtesy: diio

diio is AI that understands what business conversations are trying to achieve — and helps teams act on them.

It analyzes meetings, calls, WhatsApp, and other customer interactions to identify what matters: customer needs, objections, commitments, risks, buying signals, and next steps.

Instead of simply recording or summarizing conversations, diio understands their context and objective. It evaluates what happened against your team’s playbooks, identifies whether the conversation is moving in the right direction, and helps decide what should happen next.

Across thousands of interactions, diio turns unstructured conversation data into actionable intelligence teams can actually use.

Built for the complexity of real-world business conversations, diio is helping companies turn AI from a passive observer into an active part of how revenue teams understand customers, make decisions, and move opportunities forward.

[Try it for free](https://www.diio.com/us/starter-diio?utm_source=ai_valley&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ai_valley_2026&utm_content=2026-09-21&utm_term=main_ad_starter)

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

Tweet:  (https://twitter.com/CompleteSkeptic/status/2099925682726002904?s=20)

**One of ChatGPT’s inventors thinks AI talks too much** - former OpenAI researcher Diogo Almeida, who helped build ChatGPT and invent RLHF, has [launched](https://typesafe.ai/blog/introducing-system-one-models-and-jev) Jev. It’s an AI model built for software rather than humans, so instead of writing text it spits out decisions + probabilities.

Turns out removing language makes things pretty cheap. Jev costs just over $0.04 per million input tokens, compared to $10 for GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1, while outputs are apparently so cheap they’re just making them free. They also claim responses take 70-500ms instead of seconds/minutes for traditional LLMs.

TypeSafe calls Jev a first-of-its-kind “System One” model, focused more on intuition than reasoning. You give it some context and define the possible outputs in advance, then Jev picks an answer + tells you how confident it is. It can also answer a bunch of questions in parallel, without one answer affecting the others.

_Here are some things built using Jev:_

Tweet:  (https://twitter.com/marcus_lowe/status/2101476399488160013?s=20)

Tweet:  (https://twitter.com/romanbuildsaas/status/2100891604735099103?s=20)

It’s not replacing ChatGPT. Jev doesn’t write emails, code or explanations. The bet is that a lot of software doesn’t need an AI to talk to it anyway. It just needs something cheap and fast that can classify, route, score or decide what happens next.


----------

----------
# TRENDING TOOLS


--------------------
* [Acrobat's new AI](https://business.adobe.com/products/acrobat-business.html) - helps you understand documents faster, turning dense reports into visual summaries, interactive reports, podcasts, and audio experiences you can take anywhere ~^(sponsored)^~

* [Astra for Law](https://openai.com/index/astra-for-law/) - OpenAI's GPT-6 setup for legal research and drafting

* [ChatGPT in Word](https://x.com/ChatGPT/status/2100661995762798916) - users can now add OpenAI's flagship chatbot to Microsoft Word for turning notes into drafts, proofreading and suggesting edits

* [Hemmingway-1](https://huggingface.co/Altworld/Hemmingway-1) - a model based on Qwen3.8-27B that promises to sound and write like a person more than any other model around

* [Laya](https://x.com/mizorewww/status/2101473552956555427?s=20) - a version 50 times faster than Jev, running on your device

* [Qwen-Image-2.1](https://x.com/Alibaba_Qwen/status/2101659302792679789?s=20) - the most balanced and cost-effective image generation model in the Qwen-Image series

* [Pion](https://andonlabs.com/pion) - agents for running fully autonomous companies

* [Tables](https://www.tables.so/) - finds you sales leads from a database of 300M+ verified contacts when you describe your ideal customer in plain English

* [Runway Enhance Frame Rate](https://x.com/runwayml/status/2100620377005203564) - a frame interpolation model that converts any footage to the specs users need


----------

----------
# WHAT I'M CONSUMING


--------------------
